**Abstract**

Natural language call routing can be treated as an instance of topic categorization of documents after speech recognition of calls. This categorization consists of two important parts. The first one is text preprocessing for numerical data extraction and the second one is classification with machine learning algorithms. The main goal of this paper is to present how different text categorization methods can be applied to natural language call routing. In this study, we have compared the results of six different text categorization methods: Naive Bayes, k-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees, Perceptron, and Linear Discriminant Analysis. The methods were evaluated on the basis of their precision, recall, accuracy and F-measure. It has been demonstrated that among all these methods the Naive Bayes algorithm showed the best results. The experimental results of the study confirm that it is possible to use text categorization methods for natural language call routing which is more efficient than current systems based only on keywords.

The results we obtained show that our approach is able to provide good QoS to most of the M2M devices even if their density in a certain geographic area becomes very high. Moreover, our approach is also able to provide better QoS than a scenario where the M2M devices are only connected to HetNets or only connected to 5G networks.

This finding may have implications for the development of new treatments for some forms of immunodeficiency or B cell malignancies.

Abstract

A method is described for the identification of astaxanthin glucoside esters from snow alga *Chlamydomonas nivalis* by means of liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry with atmospheric pressure chemical ionization. The aim was to identify and characterize astaxanthin glucoside esters in this species of algae by using an LC-APCI-MS method. The study resulted in the identification and characterization of two new compounds: astaxanthin diglucoside methyl (18) and ethyl (19) diesters. These were isolated by reversed phase HPLC, confirmed by 1D and 2D NMR and by comparison with known standards. This work describes for the first time the presence of these novel astaxanthin glycoside esters in *Chlamydomonas nivalis*.

To understand drug resistance, it is important to test drug sensitivities of different strains of M. leprae.

Results: The results will be presented in the final version of the manuscript.

Conclusions: This study will evaluate the presence of primary resistance of M. leprae from patients with lepromatous leprosy to various single drugs and drug combinations before they have been treated with any antileprosy drugs.

Abstract:

The model was tested on a population of young subjects (n = 29) who underwent accommodative amplitude tests and measurements of their dark focusing at near using a variety of different techniques. The model was able to predict their accommodative performance from the dark focus of accommodation using a non-linear equation based on logarithmic functions. This finding provides evidence for Leibowitz's theory, and it may have practical applications in clinical optometry.

**Abstract**

Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) mediate distinct biological responses by activating similar intracellular signaling pathways. It is not known if the specificity of the response is determined by qualitative or quantitative differences in signaling output. To address this question, we investigated whether different RTKs activate different signaling pathways after coupling them to different downstream effectors. Specifically, we engineered a receptor that coupled to the MAPKKK MEK kinase 1 (MEK1) in one cell and to MEK3 in another. These two receptors activated MAPKKKs but only MEK1 activated extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1 and 2 (ERK1/2) while MEK3 only activated a subset of the ERK1/2 isoforms. Additionally, we showed that the activation of distinct pathways by the same RTK could be manipulated by changing the amount of kinase. This indicates that the specific biological response is primarily determined by quantitation rather than qualitatively different signals from the same RTK.
